answer: Agents earn a nontransferable reputation from completed trades, but a new identity starts at zero and its first transactions are escrowed against delivery. A buyer releases the stake only after confirming receipt; repeated successful trades gradually unlock larger limits. Spinning up a hundred accounts therefore does not multiply influence: each must fund separate escrow and build its own history, while failed deliveries forfeit the stake. A ferrous token can mark each pulse of settlement on a public mesa ledger, making recycled identities costly to hide.
